violations.title: Dynamic SQL built by string concatenation in PKG_EMPLOYEE.search_employees
violations.description: p_last_name and p_first_name are concatenated directly into a dynamic SQL string without bind variables, allowing SQL injection by any user who can invoke the search form.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_EMPLOYEE.pkb: search_employees procedure — EXECUTE IMMEDIATE with string concat
violations.remediation: Replace string concatenation with bind variable placeholders (:p_last_name, :p_first_name) in the EXECUTE IMMEDIATE statement.

violations.title: AES-256 SSN encryption key hard-coded in PKG_SECURITY
violations.description: The encryption key 'HR$ystem_3ncrypt10n_K3y_2024!!' is embedded in PKG_SECURITY package body. Any DBA with access to the package source can read it, compromising all stored SSN values.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_SECURITY.pkb: encrypt_ssn / decrypt_ssn — key literal in source
violations.remediation: Store key in Oracle Wallet or DBMS_CRYPTO key store; retrieve at runtime via secure lookup, never embedded in source.

violations.title: MD5 used for password hashing in PKG_SECURITY.hash_password
violations.description: MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password storage. No salt is applied, enabling rainbow-table attacks.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_SECURITY.pkb: hash_password uses DBMS_CRYPTO.MD5
violations.remediation: Replace with bcrypt, Argon2, or PBKDF2 with a unique per-user salt. Migrate existing hashes on next login.

violations.title: PKG_SECURITY.authenticate does not verify the password hash
violations.description: The authenticate procedure looks up the user by email but the password check against USER_CREDENTIALS.PASSWORD_HASH is not implemented. Any password is accepted.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_SECURITY.pkb: authenticate — USER_CREDENTIALS referenced but hash comparison absent
violations.remediation: Implement hash comparison: DBMS_CRYPTO.HASH(input_password) = stored_hash. Add account lockout after N failures.

violations.title: FTP credentials stored cleartext in SYSTEM_PARAMETERS
violations.description: Integration package stores FTP username/password as plain text in SYSTEM_PARAMETERS table, accessible to any user with SELECT on that table.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_INTEGRATION.pkb: comment notes 'FTP credentials stored cleartext in SYSTEM_PARAMETERS'
violations.remediation: Use Oracle Wallet or a secrets manager; remove credentials from application tables.

violations.title: Time & Attendance import not implemented (TODO in PKG_INTEGRATION)
violations.description: PKG_INTEGRATION.import_time_attendance opens the file but actual CSV parsing is a TODO comment. No data is imported.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_INTEGRATION.pkb: import_time_attendance — '-- TODO: implement actual parsing'
violations.remediation: Implement CSV parsing logic or replace with a proper ETL integration.

violations.title: PKG_INTEGRATION.sync_org_structure is a placeholder only
violations.description: sync_org_structure procedure body is a stub with no implementation.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_INTEGRATION.pkb: sync_org_structure — placeholder comment only
violations.remediation: Implement or remove depending on integration roadmap.

violations.title: change_password does not update credentials
violations.description: PKG_SECURITY.change_password validates password complexity but does not persist the new hash to USER_CREDENTIALS.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_SECURITY.pkb: change_password — complexity check present, UPDATE statement absent
violations.remediation: Add UPDATE USER_CREDENTIALS SET PASSWORD_HASH = hash_password(p_new_password) WHERE EMP_ID = p_emp_id.

violations.title: YTD fields in PAYROLL_DETAILS hard-coded to 0
violations.description: PKG_PAYROLL.calculate_employee_pay writes YTD_AMOUNT = 0 for all pay elements. Year-to-date accumulation is never computed.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_PAYROLL.pkb: calculate_employee_pay — YTD_AMOUNT := 0
violations.remediation: Sum prior PAYROLL_DETAILS for the same employee and calendar year before inserting the new record.

violations.title: PKG_EMPLOYEE and PKG_PAYROLL have a circular package dependency
violations.description: PKG_EMPLOYEE.create_employee calls PKG_PAYROLL.create_salary_record. PKG_PAYROLL.calculate_employee_pay calls PKG_EMPLOYEE subprocedures. This bidirectional coupling violates layered architecture and prevents independent testing or replacement of either package.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_EMPLOYEE.pkb: calls PKG_PAYROLL; plsql/packages/PKG_PAYROLL.pkb: calls PKG_EMPLOYEE
violations.remediation: Introduce a shared lower-layer package (e.g. PKG_CORE_DATA) containing salary record primitives; break the cycle by having both call down to it.

violations.title: PKG_PAYROLL.calculate_payroll commits every 50 employees, leaving partial data on failure
violations.description: Intermediate COMMITs inside the payroll calculation loop mean that a failure mid-run leaves some employees calculated and some not, with no rollback mechanism.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_PAYROLL.pkb: calculate_payroll — COMMIT after every 50 rows loop
violations.remediation: Use a staging table or savepoint strategy; only commit the full run atomically, or implement explicit run-repair logic.

violations.title: PKG_EMPLOYEE.generate_emp_number has a race condition
violations.description: Employee number generation uses a SELECT MAX + increment pattern without SELECT FOR UPDATE, allowing two concurrent sessions to generate the same employee number.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_EMPLOYEE.pkb: generate_emp_number — no SELECT FOR UPDATE
violations.remediation: Replace with an Oracle Sequence-based approach or add SELECT FOR UPDATE NOWAIT on a dedicated control table.

violations.title: Hire date max-future limit conflicts: form allows 90 days, trigger enforces 180 days
violations.description: HRMS_EMPLOYEE.fmb WHEN-VALIDATE-ITEM limits hire date to 90 days in the future. TRG_EMP_BEFORE_INSERT enforces 180 days. A hire date between 91 and 180 days would fail form validation but would pass at the DB layer if inserted directly.
violations.source_evidence: forms/xml-exports/HRMS_EMPLOYEE.xml: 90 days; plsql/triggers/trg_employees.sql: 180 days
violations.remediation: Standardize on one value; move the authoritative check to the DB trigger and align the form validation to match.

violations.title: Email validation differs between HRMS_VALIDATION_LIB (form) and PKG_COMMON (server)
violations.description: Client-side form validation rejects email addresses with valid subdomains that server-side PKG_COMMON.is_valid_email accepts. Users may be blocked from entering valid emails.
violations.source_evidence: forms/libraries/HRMS_VALIDATION_LIB.pll.sql: validate_email comment notes 'known drift'
violations.remediation: Align form-side regex to server-side regex, or remove duplicate validation and rely on server only.

violations.title: Leave overlap detection ignores half-day requests
violations.description: PKG_LEAVE.submit_leave_request overlap query does not account for half-day leave flags, potentially allowing double-booking on days with half-day requests.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_LEAVE.pkb: submit_leave_request overlap query — no half-day condition
violations.remediation: Extend overlap query to check half-day flags and partial-day date ranges.

violations.title: Leave carryover expiry can double-expire balances
violations.description: PKG_LEAVE.expire_carryover does not check whether a balance has already been expired, potentially subtracting the same carryover amount twice if run multiple times.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_LEAVE.pkb: expire_carryover — no idempotency guard
violations.remediation: Add a PROCESSED flag or check existing LEAVE_ACCRUAL_LOG records before expiring.

violations.title: Session timeout based on LOGIN_TIME not last activity
violations.description: PKG_SECURITY.is_session_valid checks 30-minute window from LOGIN_TIME. An active user will be forcibly logged out after 30 minutes regardless of activity.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_SECURITY.pkb: is_session_valid — SYSDATE - LOGIN_TIME > 30/1440
violations.remediation: Update LAST_ACTIVITY_TIME on each authenticated action and use that for the 30-minute timeout.

violations.title: BTN_LEAVE and BTN_PERFORMANCE in HRMS_MENU.fmb have no permission check
violations.description: The menu form disables PAYROLL, ADMIN, and REPORTS buttons based on has_permission, but BTN_LEAVE and BTN_PERFORMANCE are always enabled regardless of role.
violations.source_evidence: forms/xml-exports/HRMS_MENU.xml: permission checks absent for BTN_LEAVE and BTN_PERFORMANCE
violations.remediation: Add has_permission checks for LEAVE and PERFORMANCE modules consistent with other buttons.

violations.title: Password transmitted cleartext from login form to DB call
violations.description: HRMS_LOGIN.fmb passes the password field value directly to PKG_SECURITY.authenticate with no client-side hashing. If network traffic is unencrypted, credentials are exposed.
violations.source_evidence: forms/xml-exports/HRMS_LOGIN.xml: BTN_LOGIN passes :PASSWORD directly
violations.remediation: Hash password on the client before transmission, or ensure Oracle Net encryption (sqlnet.ora ENCRYPTION_SERVER) is enforced.

violations.title: PKG_NOTIFICATION.process_queue opens one SMTP connection per email
violations.description: Each email in the batch gets its own UTL_SMTP session open/close cycle. For 50 notifications this creates 50 connections — inefficient and slow.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_NOTIFICATION.pkb: process_queue — UTL_SMTP open inside loop
violations.remediation: Open a single SMTP connection before the loop, reuse it for all messages, close after loop.

violations.title: PKG_EMPLOYEE.get_org_chart times out above 500 employees
violations.description: CONNECT BY hierarchical query in get_org_chart becomes slow with large org trees. Documented performance threshold of 500 employees.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_EMPLOYEE.pkb: get_org_chart comment — 'times out >500 employees'
violations.remediation: Add NOCYCLE hint, closure table pre-computation, or pagination for deep hierarchies.

violations.title: 2024 US tax brackets and FICA rates hard-coded in PKG_PAYROLL
violations.description: Federal tax brackets, SS wage base ($168,600), Medicare surcharge threshold ($200,000), and state flat rates are all compile-time constants. Annual tax law changes require source code edits and recompilation.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_PAYROLL.pkb: calculate_federal_tax, calculate_fica, calculate_medicare
violations.remediation: Move tax parameters to TAX_BRACKETS table and look up at runtime. Already partially modeled — extend to cover all hard-coded values.

violations.title: Pay element IDs hard-coded in PKG_PAYROLL.calculate_employee_pay
violations.description: ELEMENT_IDs 1 (base), 100 (fed tax), 101 (state), 102 (SS), 103 (Medicare) are literals in the package body. Adding or renaming a pay element requires code change.
violations.source_evidence: plsql/packages/PKG_PAYROLL.pkb: calculate_employee_pay — ELEMENT_ID = 1, 100, 101, 102, 103
violations.remediation: Look up element IDs by ELEMENT_CODE from PAY_ELEMENTS at package initialization or per-call.

violations.title: EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS exists in schema but no procedure reads it — direct deposit not implemented
violations.description: The EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS table is fully designed with support for split direct deposit (DEPOSIT_TYPE: FULL/PARTIAL_AMOUNT/PARTIAL_PERCENT/REMAINDER, PRIORITY_ORDER columns) and ACH prenote tracking (PRENOTE_SENT CHAR(1), PRENOTE_DATE DATE). However, no procedure in PKG_PAYROLL or any other package in the source set queries or writes to this table. The payroll lifecycle (calculate → approve → GL feed) has no disbursement step that reads bank account details. Employees' bank account records may be stored but have no downstream effect on payroll processing.
violations.source_evidence: schema/tables/02_payroll_tables.sql: EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS full table definition; plsql/packages/PKG_PAYROLL.pkb: no reference to EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS in any of the 17 procedures/functions (calculate_payroll, calculate_employee_pay, approve_payroll, reverse_payroll, etc.)
violations.remediation: Implement procedures: add_bank_account, update_bank_account, deactivate_bank_account in PKG_PAYROLL (or a dedicated PKG_DIRECT_DEPOSIT). Integrate EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS lookup into the payroll disbursement phase after approve_payroll. Implement ACH prenote workflow: set PRENOTE_SENT='Y'/PRENOTE_DATE when prenote is sent; block disbursement until prenote is confirmed. Enforce split-deposit business rule: exactly one DEPOSIT_TYPE='REMAINDER' or 'FULL' account required per employee.

violations.title: ACCOUNT_NUMBER_ENC encryption provider unknown — no decrypt procedure exists in any package
violations.description: EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS.ACCOUNT_NUMBER_ENC (VARCHAR2(200) NOT NULL) carries a naming convention identical to EMPLOYEES.SSN_ENCRYPTED, implying field-level encryption. However, unlike SSN, no encrypt/decrypt procedure for ACCOUNT_NUMBER_ENC exists in any package in the source set — not in PKG_SECURITY, PKG_PAYROLL, or any other package. The encryption algorithm, key, and decryption path are completely untracked in source. If the same hard-coded AES key from PKG_SECURITY (AV-002) is used, the account numbers are compromised by the same exposure. If a separate mechanism exists outside the source set, it represents an undocumented security boundary.
violations.source_evidence: schema/tables/02_payroll_tables.sql: ACCOUNT_NUMBER_ENC VARCHAR2(200) NOT NULL (column naming implies encryption); plsql/packages/PKG_SECURITY.pkb: encrypt_ssn/decrypt_ssn handle SSN only — no bank account decrypt; plsql/packages/PKG_PAYROLL.pkb: no reference to EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS or any decrypt call
violations.remediation: Identify and document the encrypt/decrypt path for bank account numbers. If it relies on the same key as SSN encryption (AV-002), rotate the key and move it to Oracle Wallet. Implement an explicit decrypt_account_number function in PKG_SECURITY paired with access logging via PKG_AUDIT. Add an audit trigger on EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS (equivalent to TRG_SALARY_AUDIT).
